newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down on bank and finance sales.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down on bank and finance sales.

text.p: Thai stocks ended down on Tuesday as concerns that domestic interest rates were set to rise saw selling pressure mount on bank and finance stocks, traders said.
The SET Index fell 8.05 points, or 1.14 percent, to 700.15. The SET-50 ended down 0.78 points, or 1.51 percent, to 50.87. Turnover was 2.82 billion baht.
Concern that rising rates could crimp corporate earnings in interest rate sensitive sectors this year triggered foreign investor selling of bank and finance stocks, analysts said.

"I think there was some portfolio adjustment by foreign investors who sold banks and finance and bought some telecoms and chemical stocks," said Vason Thangkavivit, head of research at Pacific Finance and Securities.
The shift saw select telecom stocks approach their single day 10 percent daily limit up. Shares of Thai Telephone gained two baht to 23.25 and National Petrochemical two to 22.25.

"I think this switch in focus could be repeated in the medium term as prospects for bank earnings in 1997 don't look as good and finance firms are facing tight liquidity and high interbank rates," Vason said.
Investors fear the Bank of Thailand committment to absorb liquidity to help protect the weak baht has put pressure for a longer term rates to rise, analysts said.
The market was not concerned about reports China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping's health was deteriorating.
Finance stocks lost 1.18 percent and banks 1.68 percent, while building materials fell on results concerns.
Siam Cement lost 20 baht to 620 on concerns year end figures may fall below market expectations. Bangkok Bank shed three baht to 164 and Bank of Ayudhya dropped three to 56.
